overview: A two-page Department of State list of papers indexing diplomatic reports from 1931–1939 concerning the governor-general and senior government officials of Japanese-ruled Taiwan (Formosa). The listed records cover resignations following the Wushe (Musha) Incident, changes among high colonial officials, the appointment and later resignation of Kenzo Nakagawa, the succession of Admiral Seizo Kobayashi, and a proposed gubernatorial trip to the South Seas.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning the Governor of Formosa
subfiles.about: An index summarizes diplomatic reports from 1931–1939 about changes in Taiwan’s colonial leadership and a proposed gubernatorial journey to the South Seas.
subfiles.summary: The first page lists reports on the resignation of a governor-general following the Wushe Incident, resignations among senior Taiwan Government officials, the appointment of Kenzo Nakagawa, and Nakagawa’s replacement by Admiral Seizo Kobayashi. It also supplies brief source information, dates, report numbers, and a cross-reference to file 894.00/670. The second page continues the index with a 1939 report concerning a proposed trip by the governor-general to the South Seas area.

interest: The index provides a compact chronology of leadership changes in colonial Taiwan and links one governor-general’s resignation to the Wushe Incident. It is particularly useful for identifying reports that may be filed elsewhere, including the explicit cross-reference to 894.00/670, and for tracing how American diplomatic officers monitored Japanese colonial personnel and gubernatorial activity. The reference to a proposed South Seas trip also connects Taiwan’s administration with Japan’s wider regional and imperial interests.
